name: isStrictLoading
reason: Ruby reads the ivar `@strict_loading`; the port reads the `_strictLoading` field. Same single read, no branch — the whole divergence is the ivar spelling.

name: isStrictLoadingAll
reason: `@strict_loading_mode == :all` vs `strictLoadingMode.call(this) === "all"` — the port routes the ivar read through the `strictLoadingMode` accessor, which is the same read.

name: isStrictLoadingNPlusOneOnly
reason: `@strict_loading_mode == :n_plus_one_only` vs `strictLoadingMode.call(this) === "n_plus_one_only"` — the port routes the ivar read through the `strictLoadingMode` accessor, which is the same read.

name: initializeInternalsCallback
reason: Rails' body is `super; ensure_proper_type` and the generated def now realizes that super as `Core.initializeInternalsCallback.call(this, ...)`. The port holds only this module's contribution (`ensureProperType.call(this)`, inheritance.ts:824) because base.ts orchestrates the chain explicitly at both constructor branches — the composition-point pattern from #5727. Same two reaches, one of them relocated to the composition point, whose order is now machine-checked against Base's MRO by the `prism-mro:` markers there (composition.ts).

name: realInheritanceColumn
reason: `self._inheritance_column = value.to_s` (model_schema.rb:326) — same single assignment. The missing `to_s` is Ruby's Symbol-or-String coercion; the port's parameter is already typed `string | null`, and a Ruby Symbol is a JS string in trails, so there is nothing left to coerce.

name: _raiseReadonlyRecordError
reason: `raise ReadOnlyRecord, "#{self.class} is marked as readonly"` (persistence.rb:958) — same error class and message; the extra token is `self.class` spelled `this.constructor.name`, which is how the port reads a class name (JS has no `Class#to_s`).

name: _raiseRecordNotTouchedError
reason: `raise ActiveRecordError, <<~MSG.squish` (persistence.rb:962-965) — same error class and same message; the port writes the already-squished string literal, so the only missing token is the `squish` Ruby heredoc idiom has no counterpart for.

name: isNewRecord
reason: Ruby reads the ivar `@new_record`; the port reads the `_newRecord` field. Same single read — the whole divergence is the ivar spelling.

name: isPersisted
reason: `!(@new_record || @destroyed)` vs `!this._newRecord && !this._destroyed` — De Morgan over the same two ivar reads, still bypassing any subclass override of new_record?/destroyed? as Rails does.

name: isPreviouslyNewRecord
reason: Ruby reads the ivar `@previously_new_record`; the port reads the `_previouslyNewRecord` field. Same single read — the whole divergence is the ivar spelling.

name: aliasTracker
reason: `ActiveRecord::Associations::AliasTracker.create(model.connection_pool, table.name, joins, aliases)` (relation.rb:1308) vs `AliasTracker.create(this.model.connectionPool(), this.table.name, joins, aliases)` (relation.ts:6349) — same call, same four arguments in order. The only differing tokens are the `ActiveRecord::Associations::` constant path, which the port reaches through an import.

name: isAlreadyInScope
reason: `@delegate_to_model && registry.current_scope(model, true)` (relation.rb:1338) — the port is the same conjunction over the same two reads; the divergence is the ivar spelling `@delegate_to_model` vs the `delegateToModel` field.

name: findNthWithLimit
reason: Spelling-only. Rails' `records[index, limit]` (finder_methods.rb) generates as `idxGet(records, index, limit)` because codegen cannot know the receiver is an Array; the port writes the same slice as `records.slice(...)`. The only other differing token is Ruby's `offset.zero?`, which the port spells as a numeric comparison. Every remaining token matches in order.

name: findTakeWithLimit
reason: `records.take(limit)` (finder_methods.rb:592) vs `records.slice(0, limit)` — `Array#take(n)` is `slice(0, n)`. The `loaded?` guard, the else arm `limit(limit).to_a`, and their order all match.
